report:
The exact retained partial theorem is justified: the stated geometric-origin surfaces admit a genuine mixed E1 Monge–Ampère operator and arbitrary-support finite-dual-energy existence and uniqueness. The higher-dimensional conclusion remains conditional on both specified resolution assumptions. The argument does not close original P16.3.

The geometric scope is correct. A normal integral curve over a perfect characteristic-p field supplies the required DVR and its nontrivially valued completion. Smoothness and geometric integrality survive the stated base change. The total dimension for both resolution applications is 1+2=3. GJKM Theorem 6.3 supplies precisely both inputs; its cited foundations need not be reproved under the task's permission. Theorem 8.2 applies to any ample model curvature class, including an L that does not descend to the originally chosen function-field variety. Its finite-extension argument concerns envelopes and is not used to descend unbounded operators or measures. The reference construction uses a model of a power of L and its metric root; pulling back preserves nefness, and the raw mass remains V=(L²). [GJKM v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1712.00980v3)

Cofinality, topology, and determination have the required scope. Model descent, resolution, embedded resolution, and completion give dominating projective SNC models without altering the generic fiber. GJKM explicitly transfers BFJ's relevant compactness and pluripotential arguments under these hypotheses. Compactness is used for sup-normalized PSH, with convergence uniform on each dual complex, equivalently pointwise on divisorial points. Fixed model Monge–Ampère measures have finite divisorial support, so their integrals are continuous in this topology. Divisorial determination is available at the final uniqueness step. Relatively ample representatives on sufficiently high models are obtained by vertical modification, not by assuming that resolution preserves ampleness. [BFJ singular metrics v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1201.0187v2)

The test-ideal application checks. Body Theorem 4.6 requires E−λD nef. Taking E=mD and λ=m makes this divisor zero; the smooth spread-out variety has total dimension d+n, which governs the generation threshold. The inclusions, subadditivity, and uniform generation used in the base-ideal estimate are exactly the required replacement properties. The bounded correction and uniform lower bound give uniform envelope convergence. GJKM's regular ample-extension argument addresses the model issue, and its Theorem 9.2 supplies orthogonality. The cited later BFJ sequence-regularization numbering corresponds to Proposition 4.5 in the supplied v1. GJKM Theorem 9.3 itself retains skeleton support; the proof does not attribute arbitrary-support existence to it.

The unbounded construction is substantive and correct. Bounded locality makes the restricted truncation measures compatible and increasing. For u≤0, the energy difference formula gives t·m(u_t){u≤−t}≤2(n+1)(e(u_{t/2})−e(u_t))→0. Hence no mass is lost. The discarded-tail estimate also has the stated constant: ∫(−u_t)m(u_t)≤(n+1)|e(u)| bounds each discarded tail, and comparing two truncations gives 2(n+1)|e(u)|‖f‖∞/t. This bound is uniform for decreasing approximants because their energies are bounded below by e(u). Together with bounded decreasing continuity, it proves approximation independence for decreasing nets, not just for a selected sequence. Bounded measures charge no pluripolar sets, and increasing restricted limits retain that property. [BFJ equation v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1201.0188v1)

The mixed construction agrees with restricted truncation. Normalize the mixed inputs u_i≤0, put h_t=n⁻¹Σu_{i,t}, and let T_t be their bounded mixed measure. Positivity of the diagonal expansion gives T_t≤(nⁿ/n!)MA(h_t). On the union of discarded sets {u_i≤−t}, h_t≤−t/n. Concavity bounds e(h_t) below by the finite energy of h=n⁻¹Σu_i, so this union has T_t-mass O(1/t). On the common retained set, bounded mixed locality gives compatibility. Thus the restricted mixed limit has mass V and equals the independently polarized weak limit. Finite interpolation of diagonal measures proves independence and positivity of the mixed coefficients.

The indispensable integrability sign is checked rather than inherited from the printed statement. BFJ-v1 Lemma 6.10's proof yields e((u+w)/2)≤[2^(n+1)(n+1)]⁻¹∫w m(u), for u,w≤0. Consequently ∫(−w)m(u)≤2^(n+1)(n+1)[−e((u+w)/2)]<∞. The displayed lemma's −w is a sign slip; its proof has the correct w. Applying this bound to convex averages and their positive mixed expansions proves mixed E1 integrability. Integration by parts and Cauchy–Schwarz then pass to E1 without merely invoking weak convergence with unbounded integrands: energies of convex combinations are polynomials of uniformly bounded degree, decreasing energy continuity gives coefficient convergence, and fixed continuous model integrands followed by monotone convergence identify the coefficients with the actual mixed integrals. This validates the surface zero-norm calculation and the higher-dimensional induction.

Locality and comparison extend correctly. Truncation locality applies on the retained strict-inequality sets; the residual pole sets have zero mass. Full mass and max(u,v−ε), followed by ε↓0, give comparison on {u<v}, including the possible equality locus. The energy directional derivative follows from the mixed polynomial formula and the discarded-tail estimate. The stronger envelope derivative is two-sided: decreasing model approximations give decreasing envelopes, their integrated derivative identity passes by dominated convergence, and replacing f by f+‖f‖∞ or f−‖f‖∞ supplies decreasing paths to u from either parameter side. The operator is invariant under the resulting constant shifts. Therefore d/dt|₀ e(Pθ(u+tf))=∫f m(u) for every continuous f.

The synthetic application has its actual hypotheses. Real vertical coefficients give the stated D; rational psh tests are uniformly dense after perturbation toward a relatively ample representative and rational approximation inside the ample cone. On each finite-dimensional space of forms, a common determination makes nefness a closed collection of curve-degree inequalities. Pullback preserves and detects these inequalities. Ample domination shows that the nef cone spans Z. Symmetry is the model intersection identity. Seminegativity follows directly from the vertical graph formula with mixed-nef weights, whose off-diagonal intersections are nonnegative. The positive Bott–Chern class assertion uses ample representatives; it does not assume an unsupported characteristic-p identification of Bott–Chern cohomology with N¹(X). Strict margins and rational maxima establish directed test maxima. Continuous envelopes and Dini convergence make this directed net converge uniformly, so GJKM orthogonality verifies the precise synthetic orthogonality condition. [Boucksom–Jonsson synthetic theory v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.01697v1)

The defect estimates and their extension are valid. Uniform concavity at the midpoint cancels the linear target terms and gives J(u,v)≤C_n(aν(u)+aν(v)); taking one potential zero bounds J(v). Lemma 2.25, with the other test equal to zero and quasi-symmetry, gives the uniform integration estimate with aν(r_j)^(1/2). A maximizing sequence exists directly from the finite supremum; Theorem 2.23 supplies its measure approximation, rather than its existence. For u∈K_C, decreasing model approximants satisfy J(u_l)→J(u)≤C. Their eventual bound C+1 is sufficient: the final constant is independent of u even though the index at which the bound holds can depend on u. Finite dual energy proves ν-integrability by monotone convergence; finite divisorial support gives integrability for m(r_j). Passing to the limit therefore yields the claimed uniform estimate over K_C and continuity of integration against ν there.

Actual attainment and realization follow. The defect bound and the compact normalized-PSH bound for ∫u m₀ put a normalized maximizing sequence in one compact K_C. A convergent subnet, energy upper semicontinuity, and the established integral continuity produce an actual E1 maximizer. No sequential compactness is assumed. The dual-energy supremum extends from tests to E1 by decreasing approximation, giving the reverse inequality at the limit. For u_t=Pθ(u+tf), positivity of ν gives h(t)≤A=h(0). The two-sided envelope derivative forces equality of m(u) and ν against every continuous function. Multiplication by V realizes the original measure μ, without a support restriction or a measure-completion surrogate. The tangent inequality also proves that every m(u) has precisely the stated finite dual energy.

Uniqueness checks independently. Model reference changes preserve curvature and the genuine operator; the bounded energy cocycle followed by decreasing approximation gives eη(u−g)=eθ(u)−eθ(g). On a surface, equality of the diagonal measures gives Nη_u(f)+Nη_v(f)=VS=0. Nonnegativity and Cauchy–Schwarz force both cross terms with u−g to vanish, and their difference gives Nη(f)=0. In dimension n, define q_k=−∫f ddᶜf·η_u^iη_v^jη^k, i+j+k=n−1. The initial nonnegative norms sum to VS. Telescoping η^k against η_u^k and applying Cauchy–Schwarz bounds each next norm by VS plus a finite constant times the square root of preceding norms. Induction gives q_k≤C S^(2^(−k)), with V absorbed in C; in particular the claimed exponent 2^(1−n) is supported. At S=0 the induction directly gives zero at every stage. This uses only the verified mixed calculus and introduces no further resolution assertion.

The strict kernel is correct in every characteristic. For the principal special fiber Σb_iE_i, expanding D² and eliminating the diagonal intersections gives D²A^(n−1)=−Σ_{i<j}b_i b_j(E_i·E_j·A^(n−1))(a_i/b_i−a_j/b_j)². Mixed-nef weights are nonnegative; with A relatively ample, weights are strictly positive for meeting components. The generic fiber has global functions K, properness makes global model functions integral over the DVR, and normality of the DVR makes that algebra equal to the DVR. Stein factorization gives connected special fibers and hence a connected component graph. With λ=−log|π| and a_i=b_i f(x_i)/λ, the model function has value f(x_i), and its intersection pairing is λD²A^(n−1), exactly as asserted. Zero norm therefore forces a common vertex value. Keeping a divisorial anchor on refinements aligns these constants even when the ample reference changes; divisorial determination then gives u=v+c. The supplied anchor argument avoids the incorrect BFJ-v1 inference that subtracting a common model function preserves equality of suprema. [Stacks connectedness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AY8)

Harmless corrections are explicit: BFJ-v1 Lemma 6.10's displayed sign must be corrected as above; the polynomial degree in the proof of Proposition 6.12 is at most n+1, rather than its printed n; and the higher-dimensional paragraph's phrase 'initial mixed norms sum to S' must read 'VS' for its raw norm convention. These corrections change neither the stated estimates with their permitted constants nor the zero-norm conclusion. No substantial repair of the supplied argument is required.

All three canonical notes were checked. n1 accurately records the source scope, hypotheses, version changes, and skeleton restriction. n2 records the justified retained theorem and its deductions. n3's mathematical status remains partial with candidate=false; its hashes, compilation counts, and artifact history are provenance assertions, not mathematical premises certified by this review. The ancillary sources provide no indispensable replacement argument: the Boucksom–Jonsson surface endpoint cited there is trivially valued, Pille–Schneider's remark has the stated wording, and Gubler–Rabinoff expressly leaves these constructions outside its subject. Mixed characteristic, dimensions without both resolution inputs, and removal of geometric origin remain explicit original obligations.

passages.statement: Over any perfect field k, every quasi-projective k-variety Z of dimension three admits a projective morphism from a regular variety that is an isomorphism over Z's regular locus. For every regular quasi-projective k-variety Z of dimension three and proper closed subset W⊂Z, there is a projective morphism π:Z′→Z between regular quasi-projective varieties, isomorphic over Z\W, such that π⁻¹(W) is supported on a normal crossing divisor. These are GJKM1712.00980v3 Definitions 6.1–6.2 and Theorem 6.3.
passages.quote: Theorem 6.3 (Cossart-Piltant). Resolution of singularities and embedded resolution of singularities hold in dimension three over any perfect field.

passages.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic p>0. Suppose a smooth projective n-dimensional K-variety X has geometric origin from a normal d-dimensional variety B over a perfect characteristic-p field k: at a codimension-one point b, the completion of O_B,b is K°, and X is the base change of a projective k(B)-variety. If resolution of singularities in GJKM Definition 6.1 holds over k in dimension d+n, then for every closed model (1,1)-form θ with ample de Rham class and every continuous f on X analytified, Pθ(f) is continuous and uniformly approximable by θ-psh model functions. passages.statement: Let X be compact Hausdorff, D⊂C⁰(X) a dense real linear space containing constants, Z a real ordered vector space whose positive cone spans Z and is closed in its finest vector-space topology, and ddᶜ:D→Z linear and zero on constants. Suppose a nonzero symmetric n-linear signed-measure pairing on Z is positive on positive tuples, and ∫f ddᶜg∧T is symmetric and seminegative for positive mixed T. Choose ω≥0 whose class lies in the interior of the image of Z₊ in Z/ddᶜD. Use the normalized model energy e, m(v)=MAω(v), Dω={v:ω+ddᶜv≥0}, J(u,v)=e(u)−e(v)+∫(v−u)m(u), and J(v)=J(0,v). Then J is quasi-symmetric and energy is uniformly concave, with constants depending only on n. For a probability measure ν with A=sup_Dω(e(v)−∫vν)<∞ and aν(v)=A−e(v)+∫vν, one has J(u,v)≤C_n(aν(u)+aν(v)). If Dω admits directed maxima below tests and lim_{v<f}∫(f−v)m(v)=0 for every f∈D, every maximizing sequence r_j has m(r_j) converging weakly to ν and its dual energies converging to A. For A≤R and v,w,r∈Dω with J(v),J(w),J(r)≤R, |∫(v−w)(ν−m(r))|≤C_n J(v,w)^(2^(−n)) aν(r)^(1/2) R^(1/2−2^(−n)). These are Boucksom–Jonsson2307.01697v1 Theorem 1.33, Proposition 2.2, Theorem 2.23 and Lemma 2.25.

passages.statement: A proper geometrically integral scheme over a field k has H⁰(O)=k. If f:Z→S is proper, S is integral and normal with generic point ξ, Z is reduced, every generic point of an irreducible component of Z maps to ξ, and H⁰(Z_ξ,O)=κ(ξ), then f_*O_Z=O_S and f has geometrically connected fibers. These are Stacks Project Lemma 33.9.3 and Lemma 37.53.6, Tags 0366 and 0AY8.

premises: Over any perfect field k, every quasi-projective k-variety Z of dimension three admits a projective morphism from a regular variety that is an isomorphism over Z's regular locus. For every regular quasi-projective k-variety Z of dimension three and proper closed subset W⊂Z, there is a projective morphism π:Z′→Z between regular quasi-projective varieties, isomorphic over Z\W, such that π⁻¹(W) is supported on a normal crossing divisor. These are GJKM1712.00980v3 Definitions 6.1–6.2 and Theorem 6.3.

Let K be complete discretely valued, let R⊂K° be a DVR whose completion is K°, let F=Frac(R), let Y be a projective F-variety, and let X=Y×F K. Every K°-model of X is dominated by the completed base change of a projective R-model of Y. A projective K°-model dominating such a completed R-model is itself the completed base change of a dominating projective R-model. Every model function on X analytified is defined over R. This is GJKM1712.00980v3 Proposition 5.2.

Let K be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic p>0. Suppose a smooth projective n-dimensional K-variety X has geometric origin from a normal d-dimensional variety B over a perfect characteristic-p field k: at a codimension-one point b, the completion of O_B,b is K°, and X is the base change of a projective k(B)-variety. If resolution of singularities in GJKM Definition 6.1 holds over k in dimension d+n, then for every closed model (1,1)-form θ with ample de Rham class and every continuous f on X analytified, Pθ(f) is continuous and uniformly approximable by θ-psh model functions. Neither θ nor its ample class is required to descend to the originally chosen k(B)-variety. This is GJKM1712.00980v3 Theorem 8.2.

Let K, k, X, B and b satisfy the geometric-origin hypotheses of GJKM1712.00980v3 Definition 8.1, with K complete discretely valued of characteristic p>0, k perfect, dim(X)=n and dim(B)=d. Assume both resolution and embedded resolution, as defined in GJKM Definitions 6.1–6.2, over k in dimension d+n. Every projective K°-model of X is then dominated by a projective SNC model. The results and proofs of BFJ1201.0187 sections 1–7 and BFJ1201.0188 sections 3–6 carry over in this setting. Every θ-psh function, for θ with ample de Rham class, admits decreasing model approximation, including a decreasing sequence. For every continuous f, ∫(f−Pθ(f))MAθ(Pθ(f))=0. These are GJKM section 9, Corollary 9.1 and Theorem 9.2.

Let k be perfect of characteristic p>0, R a finite-type k-algebra, and Z an integral N-dimensional scheme projective over Spec(R) and smooth over k. Let D,E,H be Cartier divisors and λ≥0 rational. If H is ample and globally generated, H⁰(Z,O(mD))≠0 for some m>0, and E−λD is nef, then O(K_Z/k+E+qH)⊗τ(λ·‖D‖) is globally generated for every integer q≥N+1. Asymptotic test ideals b_m of a nonzero graded sequence of base ideals a_m satisfy a_m⊂b_m and b_mℓ⊂b_m^ℓ. For a geometric regular model whose generic line bundle admits an ample extension A, the associated ideals satisfy global generation of A^m₀⊗L^m⊗b_m for one m₀ independent of m. These are GJKM1712.00980v3 section 4, body Theorem 4.6, and the properties proved in Theorem 7.3.

Let X be smooth connected projective over a complete discretely valued field of residue characteristic zero, and θ a closed model (1,1)-form with ample de Rham class. On every sufficiently high model, θ admits a model-function modification θ+ddᶜg represented by a relatively ample class; when θ is semipositive, g can be chosen with −ε≤g≤0. θ-psh functions are finite and continuous on SNC dual complexes and are determined by their divisorial values. Their topology of uniform convergence on dual complexes equals pointwise convergence on divisorial points. For every model function ψ, u↦sup_X(u−ψ) is continuous and proper; consequently {u:sup_Xu=0} is compact. These are BFJ1201.0187v2 Proposition 5.2, Corollary 7.7 and Theorem 7.10.

In the BFJ1201.0188v1 setting of a smooth connected projective variety over a complete discretely valued field of residue characteristic zero, with semipositive model reference θ of ample class and V={θ}ⁿ, bounded θ-psh potentials have a unique positive mixed Monge–Ampère operator of mass V agreeing with model intersections and continuous along decreasing bounded approximations. Bounded locality and integration by parts hold. The energy e(u)=[(n+1)V]⁻¹Σ_j∫u(θ+ddᶜu)^jθ^(n−j), extended by infima over dominating model potentials, is increasing, concave, weakly upper semicontinuous, decreasing-continuous and satisfies e(u+c)=e(u)+c. Finite-energy potentials have full-mass nonpluripolar measures m(u)=MAθ(u)/V, no pluripolar mass, decreasing-net operator continuity, locality and comparison. For u≤0 and model f, the truncation error is at most 2(n+1)|e(u)|‖f‖∞/t. E1 potentials are integrable against each other's diagonal measures, and d/dt|₀₊e((1−t)u+tv)=∫(v−u)m(u). These are Theorem 3.1, Theorem 5.1, Proposition 6.2, Definition 6.4, Lemmas 6.7–6.10 and Propositions 6.11–6.12.

In the BFJ1201.0188v1 pluripotential framework, assume continuous envelopes and orthogonality ∫(f−Pθ(f))m(Pθ(f))=0 for every continuous f. Then e∘Pθ is Gâteaux differentiable on continuous functions. Moreover, for every u∈E1 and continuous f, Pθ(u+tf)∈E1 for every real t and the two-sided derivative at zero equals ∫f m(u). These are Theorem 7.2 and Corollary 7.3; neither assertion requires skeleton support of a target measure.
